questions.stemHtml: Patient with the history of kidney transplantation presenting with diarrhea. (Video of worms given.) The motility of the worms is given in the figure. Correct statement about the organism is:

options.label: A
options.text: Monoecious and the organism related with parthenogenesis.

options.label: B
options.text: Transmitted by intake of contaminated food and water

options.label: C
options.text: Loffler's pneumonia is not caused by the same organism

options.label: D
options.text: Body gets this infection through filariform larvae.

questions.answerText: Body gets this infection through filariform larvae.
questions.solutionHtml:
Body gets this infection through filariform larvae.
  • The video depicts Rhabditiform larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis
  • S. stercoralis is dioecious and the organism related with parthenogenesis
  • Infective form is filariform larvae (eggs give rise to larva and develop into filariform larvae)
  • Transmitted by skin penetration of filariform larvae
  • Loffler’s pneumonia caused by Ascaris and hookworms

questions.stem: Small amounts of repeated thin stools with mucus, subjective feeling of fever and lower abdominal pain, with leukocytes in stool. Which of the following is likely?
questions.solutionHtml:
Entamoeba
  • Except amoebiasis all others cause watery and non-bloody diarrhea.
  • Also, none of the other mentioned disorders apart from amoebiasis have WBCs in stool.
  • Amoebiasis can cause intermittent abdominal pain and mucous/bloody diarrhea as a part of chronic disease.
  • Fever can be seen approximately in 10–30% of patients with amoebiasis.

questions.stem: 200 people attended a party and some of them had diarrhea after 24 hours. They ate oyster, hamburger, ice cream, and potato salad. What’s the likely cause?40 ill from 50 who consumed oyster50 ill from 135 who consumed hamburger60 ill from 140 who consumed salad49 ill from 115 who consumed ice cream
questions.solutionHtml:
Vibrio parahaemolyticus

IN THIS QUES, Most guests who ate the oysters, that's why the most likely source of infection is by Vibrio parahaemolyticus.

  • V. parahaemolyticus is a capsulated vibrio with peritrichous flagella.
  • Infections with V. parahaemolyticus can result in two distinct gastrointestinal presentations (including nearly all cases in North America).
  • The most common presentation is watery diarrhea, usually occurring in conjunction with abdominal cramps, nausea, and vomiting and accompanied in 25% of cases by fever and chills.
  • Dysentery, the less common presentation, is characterized by severe abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, and bloody or mucoid stools.
  • V. parahaemolyticus contains two type III secretion systems, which directly inject toxic bacterial proteins into host cells.
  • After an incubation period of 4 hours to 4 days, symptoms develop and persist for a median of 3 days.
  • V. parahaemolyticus is linked to its ability to cause hemolysis on Wagatsuma agar), i.e., is called Kanagawa phenomenon.
  • Doxycycline, fluoroquinolones, or macrolides are preferred in this case.

questions.stem: A postrenal transplant patient presents with diarrhea after 3 months. It showed organisms measuring 2-6-micron meter and Kinyoun stain positive. Most likely it is caused by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cryptosporidium parvum
  • Opportunistic infections are extremely common post-transplant in the period starting from 1-month post-transplant to 6 months’ post-transplant.
  • Clostridium difficile is usually seen within 1-month post-transplant because of profound antibiotic use.
  • Kinyoun stain (modified acid fast) positivity rules out Balantidium.
  • Now it is between cryptosporidium and cyclo Isospora. Size (smaller, i.e., 2–6 microns) tells us that the organism is undoubtedly Cryptosporidium parvum.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:815.

questions.stem: A patient is having thick, gray coating on the throat and tonsils, followed by fever, chills, and swollen glands in the neck. Microscopic examination of nasopharyngeal or pharyngeal swab showed gram-positive organisms with a special stain. The constitutes of the stain are:

options.label: B
options.text: Toluidine blue, malachite green, glacial acetic

options.label: C
options.text: Carbol fuchsin, acid alcohol, and methylene blue

questions.answerText: Toluidine blue, malachite green, glacial acetic
questions.solutionHtml:
Toluidine blue, malachite green, glacial acetic
  • The clinical scenario depicts Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection.
  • The special staining used for Corynebacterium diphtheriae is Albert’s.
  • Albert’s solution is of two types A and B given below briefly:

Albert’s A solution

Albert’s B solution

•  Toluidine blue 0.15 g

•  Malachite green 0.20 g

•  Glacial acetic acid 1 mL

•  Alcohol (95% ethanol) 2 mL

•  Iodine 2 g

•  Potassium iodide (KI) 3 g

  • Albert’s metachromatic stains kit (K002)
  • Metachromatic Granules-Black Cytoplasm-Light green
  • Note: Neisser’s stain and Ponder’s stain are also used to demonstrate polar bodies of Corynebacterium diphtheriae.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:18

questions.stem: A newly introduced vaccine includes all, except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Influenza
  • Rota virus
  • It has been approved by the Government of India for inclusion into the UIP with the phase I launch of the vaccine in 4 states (Himachal Pradesh, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Haryana) in February 2016.
  • It is administered at age 6–15 weeks.
  • Maximum age for administering the last dose of either vaccine should be 32 weeks.

  • Dengue vaccine
  • It is known as Dengvaxia (CYD-TDV).
  • It is live recombinant as a 3-dose series on a 0/6/12 months’ schedule in Phase II clinical studies.
  • It has been registered for use in individuals 9–45 years of age living in endemic areas.
  • In April 2016, WHO Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE) on immunization recommended introduction of the vaccine only in geographic settings (national or subnational) with endemicity.

  • Malaria vaccine

  • It is known as RTS, S/AS01
  • It is the first malaria vaccine to have completed Phase III testing.
  • RTS, S is a vaccine against Plasmodium falciparum.
  • It offers no protection against P. vivax malaria
  • The vaccine is being considered as a complementary malaria control tool in Africa.
